name: Lovely Notes
author: Lucy

sections.description:
Lovely Notes adds a small, independent notebook to your WordPress site. Publish thoughts, poems, song lyrics or everyday moments without a visible post title.

The plugin interface is currently in French. Its text is translation-ready. Your notes can be written in any language, and dates follow your WordPress language and timezone settings.

Features

  • Write notes in the WordPress editor or the quick-publish widget on the dashboard.
  • Add an image, a video, or an optional external media embed.
  • Display a note reader using [lovely_notes].
  • Browse notes without reloading the whole page, on desktop and mobile.
  • Display monthly archives using [lovely_notes_archive].
  • Open a full note from the archives and copy its permanent sharing link.
  • Show video thumbnails in the archives, with a fallback when a preview is unavailable.
  • Enlarge images in a lightbox.
  • Set a maximum reading area in ordinary text lines; longer text remains available by scrolling.
  • Choose a custom name for your microblog.
  • Add an optional “Lovely Eye” link to something you want readers to discover.

No account, API key or paid service is needed to use the notebook with your own text and locally hosted media. External videos and images depend on their hosting services.

Support the author

Lovely Notes is free. If you enjoy it, you can buy the author a coffee. Donations are entirely optional and the amount is up to you. The settings page includes the same optional support link.

Shortcodes

Add a Shortcode block to a page and paste:

[lovely_notes]

This displays the newest published note, with navigation to other notes.

For the monthly archive, use:

[lovely_notes_archive]

The plugin also creates an archive page automatically. Open the plugin settings to view that page and copy either shortcode.

Optional reader attributes:

  • [lovely_notes text_lines="8"] sets the maximum reading height for this reader.
  • [lovely_notes show_name="yes"] always displays the microblog name.
  • [lovely_notes show_name="no"] hides the microblog name.
  • [lovely_notes show_date="no"] hides the publication date.
  • [lovely_notes show_media="no"] hides media attached through the plugin’s dedicated media fields; media inside the note text remains part of that text.

The default show_name="auto" displays the name when you have chosen a custom name. The class attribute can add your own CSS classes.

Only published notes without a password appear in the public reader, archives and sharing links.

External services

Lovely Notes has no built-in analytics or telemetry and does not send note text or administrator account details to an author-operated server. It makes no external media request merely because the plugin is activated. External media requests occur when an author explicitly adds external media to a note and WordPress or a visitor displays that media. The optional support link contacts PayPal only when you choose to open it.

YouTube / Google

Purpose: display author-selected videos and their archive thumbnails. WordPress may request embed metadata for the selected video URL. A visitor’s browser loads thumbnails from i.ytimg.com and players from YouTube or youtube-nocookie.com, depending on the saved embed. These requests disclose the selected video identifier and normal connection information such as the requester IP address and browser details. The hosting service may use cookies or other storage according to its own policy.

  • Terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Vimeo

Purpose: display author-selected videos and retrieve their thumbnails. The site server sends the selected video URL to Vimeo’s oEmbed service; a visitor’s browser loads the returned thumbnail and, when the note is displayed, its Vimeo player. An unlisted video’s access hash is retained when needed. Provider responses are cached for up to seven days; unsuccessful thumbnail lookups are cached for one hour. Requests expose the media URL and normal connection information to the provider.

  • Terms: https://vimeo.com/legal/
  • Privacy: https://vimeo.com/legal/privacy

PayPal.Me (optional donations)

Purpose: let users voluntarily support the plugin author. Clicking the support link opens the author’s PayPal.Me page in a new tab. The browser then sends normal connection information to PayPal. Any account or payment details you provide there are handled by PayPal. Lovely Notes does not load PayPal scripts, images or payment forms, and does not send WordPress account details or note content to PayPal.

  • Terms: https://www.paypal.com/fr/legalhub/paypal/paypalme-tnc
  • Privacy: https://www.paypal.com/fr/legalhub/paypal/privacy-full

Other externally hosted media

Images, video files and manually inserted iframes contact the host selected by the author. Standard WordPress embeds use the oEmbed providers enabled by WordPress or other installed plugins. Requests may include the selected media URL and normal connection information. Check the selected host’s terms and privacy policy before using its media. WordPress’s built-in embed documentation: https://wordpress.org/documentation/article/embeds/

Use locally hosted media to avoid third-party media hosts. Lovely Notes does not itself provide a visitor cookie-consent interface; configure your site’s consent tools where needed for your selected embeds and external thumbnails.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin, select the Lovely Notes ZIP, and install it.
  2. Activate Lovely Notes.
  3. Publish a note from the Lovely Notes menu, or use the quick-publish widget on the dashboard.
  4. Edit the page where you want the reader to appear. Add a Shortcode block, paste [lovely_notes], then publish or update the page. In the classic editor, paste the shortcode directly into the page content.
  5. Visit Lovely Notes > Settings (“Reglages” in the French interface) to choose the microblog name and the number of visible lines. You can also copy the shortcodes there.
  6. Use the automatically created archive page, or place [lovely_notes_archive] in a page of your choice.

When replacing an existing version, use the same upload procedure and accept WordPress’s replacement prompt. Notes, media, settings and the existing archive page are preserved. Clear your page cache after updating if older assets are still displayed.
sections.faq:
Which shortcode should I use?

Use [lovely_notes] for the reader and [lovely_notes_archive] for the monthly archives. Both are visible, with copy buttons, in the plugin settings.

How do I share one note?

Open the note from the archives and use the copy-link button. The link selects that note by its permanent ID, so publishing newer notes does not change the selection. Draft, private, password-protected and deleted notes are unavailable through public sharing links.

Does the line limit delete or truncate my text?

No. The complete text stays saved. The setting defines a maximum height equivalent to ordinary lines, including paragraph spacing, and scrolling reveals the rest. The default is 10 lines, with a range of 1 to 100.

Can I rename the notebook?

Yes. Choose a name in the settings. The plugin remains named Lovely Notes, while your custom name appears in the reader and administration. The automatic archive title follows the name only if you have not already edited that title yourself. Existing addresses stay unchanged.

How do video previews work?

YouTube thumbnails and thumbnails supplied by supported WordPress video providers, including Vimeo, can appear in archive cards. A locally hosted video uses its poster or Media Library thumbnail when available. Otherwise, a static frame is loaded near the viewport, without starting playback. If a preview cannot be loaded, a video symbol remains and the note still opens normally.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

The plugin does not delete notes, uploaded media, settings or the archive page. Its shortcodes stop working while it is inactive. Back up your site before removing data yourself.
sections.changelog:
0.7.5

  • Removed direct script output from administration header hooks.
  • Writing invitations now use native WordPress block editor settings, including for iframe editors.

0.7.4

  • Added an optional “buy the author a coffee” link in the plugin settings and directory readme.
  • Documented the user-initiated PayPal.Me link and confirmed the WordPress.org contributor account.

0.7.3

  • Added copyable shortcodes and setup instructions in the settings.
  • Improved documentation, licensing, public input handling and archive excerpts.

Earlier releases are documented in changelog.txt.
